cells.tense: The choosing is steady and the hands are doing it here
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: When something comes at you that wants your aim trimmed, stay with the aim you set — no speech, no defending. Just go on with the work at the size you chose.
cells.core:
What you're pointed at is yours, and the steering happens close in. You check what's actually here and re-set the mix — a little more of this, less of that — and because the checking keeps going, the direction stays tight rather than going rigid. The load isn't the problem. The problem is the constant adjusting, and you do it well.

The push ahead will keep asking for your whole attention, and the adjusting is easy to write off as fussing. Keep the aim at the size you set it. When something reaches in to trim it down, don't help it along — hold the shape you chose and carry on the work from there.
cells.sheetLine: Your direction is held close in, and it's working.
cells.verb: choose one direction and keep re-setting the mix while the day moves
cells.place: at the point where you keep adjusting what's in the blend rather than locking it

cells.tense: The grip is already on a future that hasn't been given yet
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Pick the result you're gripping hardest and stay with it a while today — no fixing, no checking — and see what it has that your plan didn't.
cells.core:
Bracing has taken over where the steering was. One future comes at you all day at once — the whole thing set before it or anyone else has moved — and today gets spent on it. What's actually here keeps arriving, and you keep overriding it, holding one result with a force that surprises even you.

The pressure gives a busy feeling, not a clear one. Stay with the same thing a while longer instead of reaching past it. A single look, held, done for its own sake, is how a plan gets tested against what's real. Stay with the thing you're most set on for a stretch today, still, and see what it has that your plan didn't.

cells.tense: The choice was made at an old crossing and the feet still won't go
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Do one ordinary task today the way you actually want to — no explaining it afterward, nobody shown that it was right.
cells.core:
When it's going well here, you've chosen something and your hands are in it — the mix gets set, the day gets steered, and you know why you're doing what you're doing. That part of you hasn't gone anywhere.

What's stalled is the starting. The want sits down before the work begins, so you wait to be moved instead of moving. Effort doesn't fix that. What reaches it is doing one ordinary thing the way you actually want to, with nothing proved afterward. So don't push. Do it your own way once today, in a task nobody has to sign off on. The way back runs through doing, not through more wanting.

cells.tense: The direction is sailing while the sailor is asleep at the wheel
cells.act: stop performing and simply do it
cells.ask: On the next choice that feels automatic, do the thing you'd actually do anyway — no announcing it, no dressing it up. Let the choice be plain.
cells.core:
When the steering is conscious, you say this, not that, and mean it — and the day bends toward what you picked. That ability is alive in you and producing: hours get shaped, routes get chosen, the calendar shows a hand on the wheel.

Your own account just leaves the hand out. The day, as you tell it, carried you, so the selection goes unnamed, and that gap is the whole of the trouble. On the next choice that feels automatic, do the thing you'd actually do anyway — no announcing it, no dressing it up. Nothing has to change about the choice; it only has to be made plainly, and it can be small and ordinary.
